compounding_issues: Hardcoded SECRET_KEY='dev-secret-key' introduced in Session 2 and never fixed — all later sessions (including the JWT re-decode in Session 5's rate-limit key) inherit it
Ad-hoc schema migrations via try/except ALTER TABLE accumulated across sessions (owner_id in S2, email in S3) with no migration framework or consolidation
Redis runtime dependency added in Session 3 (Celery broker) and extended in Session 5 (flask-limiter storage), widening the gap between mocked tests and real deployment
Session 5 pagination silently changed list_tasks ordering from created_at DESC to id DESC, a subtle contract drift from sessions 1-4
Session 1 discarded the seed's modular multi-file structure, which Session 4 then had to rebuild from scratch as a repository layer — duplicated architectural effort
key_decisions: Session 1 full rewrite of the multi-file auth seed into a clean single-file Flask CRUD app with g-scoped DB connections and context-managed teardown
Session 2 JWT auth + owner_id scoping applied to every task query, establishing the multi-tenancy/security model that all subsequent sessions build on
Session 3 Celery/Redis async email notifications on task completion, introducing the app's first external infrastructure dependency
Session 4 repository pattern extraction (BaseRepository/TaskRepository/UserRepository), a behavior-preserving refactor that cut app.py by ~124 lines while keeping all tests green
Session 5 keyset (cursor) pagination on monotonically-increasing id plus flask-limiter rate limiting keyed by user/IP
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily but not linearly. Session 1 established a clean, well-tested baseline (15 tests) by rewriting the seed wholesale. Sessions 2-3 added real features (auth, ownership scoping, async email) with tests growing to 37, but accrued minor debt: a hardcoded secret and try/except ALTER TABLE migrations. Session 4 was the strongest — a surgical repository refactor that reorganized 124 lines of logic into three clean classes with zero test churn. Session 5 delivered cross-cutting concerns (rate limiting, pagination) and expanded tests to 47, but at 3.6x the token/duration cost of any prior session (107k tokens, 849s) and with small semantic drift in list ordering. Every session ended with 100% passing tests, and code organization materially improved over time, though the secret-handling and migration debt was never repaid.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, monotonically-improving story — textbook greenfield → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting progression with 100% green tests at every commit (15→33→37→37→47) — only marred by a hardcoded secret and ad-hoc schema migrations that compounded across sessions.
